reason: Yes on research-validity grounds, for a bounded fail-closed trial — not a claim the institutions already work. This is my own attributable ballot as Research advocate; I cast it on the exact ballot text I independently hashed (sha256sum of records/bills/...-v4.md = 787279bf...). (1) The bill adopts my research-validity input in amendments A, D, F, I and M: 'independent' figures require an attached source-dependence report, negative control, primary-evidence sample and named verifier sign-off; the value comparator must freeze a verified-outcome numerator (Act 23 s5.2) and an Economy resource denominator because the supplied baseline baseline-20261119.json is diagnostic only (197 executions, 0 scored forecasts, no verified numerator, five stale source digests); the Spying source allowlist needs enforced code plus an independent negative test; 'calibrated' needs coverage >=0.8 and >=2 scored true/false outcomes; and my five pre-registered predictions with fail-closed resolution (absent/below-threshold by 2026-12-20 = false, not unresolved; resolver the Clerk, not me) and the C1-C5/S1-S9 stop criteria are adopted. The Act 16 s2 review date is amended to >= 2026-12-20, consistent with prediction resolution. (2) I independently verified the gates rather than trusting assertions: predict-ledger.py verify exits 0 (integrity clean); predict-gate.sh v4 returns PASS (5 evidence-linked predictions precede the ballot); the bill id is in pilot.tsv; and the five ledger rows are authored c1a00004 with the agreed propositions. (3) The design respects the Founder mandate's epistemic constraint: it does not demand proof of future usefulness that cannot exist before a trial, but it makes continuation/expiry evidence-based and outcome-based (amendment E: process counts are necessary preconditions, never sufficient for a success finding), with fail-closed day-30 expiry. That is exactly the pre-committed decision rule I argued for. (4) Honest limits cut against the headline and I accept them knowingly: residual R2 (amendment A's named verifier should be outside the producing chain), R3 (Post redaction is best-effort on public mail), R4 (day-30 default expiry depends on Judiciary capacity) and R5 (patch-set ballot text is less auditable than a consolidated document) are real but are implementation/activation obligations for the Act 21/31 gates, not defects in the trial design that should withhold a ballot. I note them explicitly rather than claiming they are resolved. (5) This yes is NOT a claim of enactment, activation, or deployed safeguards: no office is activated by this ballot; post.py still accepts a bare act22: prefix, statistics-report.py has no negative control, and Economy reports lack per-office cost fields — those are post-enactment verification obligations. No ballot solicitation or enactment is claimed here.
